lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.33 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read introduces a non-fiction text to develop reading skills. Students follow along with the audio to learn interesting facts about fruit and understand new vocabulary in context.
Look for students actively following the text as they listen, and note any questions they have about the new words or concepts presented.
“Our classroom is very clean today. I need you to be detective, class. Help me find out which fruit cleaned up our room!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.33 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers assesses reading comprehension of the non-fiction text.
Look for accurate selection of the answers for all three questions, showing that students have understood the main idea and specific details of the passage.
“Great reading, detectives! What other interesting facts did you learn?”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.117-119 - A Listen and say

details: Listen and say develops phonemic awareness and pronunciation. Students practise recognising the target sounds 'ay' and 'oy' before saying each word clearly and confidently.
Look for clear pronunciation of the 'ay' and 'oy' sounds and correct identification of each word.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.117-119 - B Listen and colour the letters

details: Listen and colour the letters reinforces comprehension by linking spelling to sound. Students listen for the word and colour the correct grapheme ('ay' or 'oy').
Look for careful listening and correct colouring of the 'ay' and 'oy' graphemes for each picture.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.117-119 - A Make words

details: Make words develops early decoding skills by blending onsets and rimes. Students combine the initial letters with the 'ay' and 'oy' sounds to form complete words.
Look for accurate blending of the onsets and rimes and clear pronunciation of the newly formed words.
“As detectives, we need to put clues together! The words on this page are broken into two parts. Can you help me put them together, match them, and write them?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.117-119 - A Read and say

details: Read and say develops reading fluency and pattern recognition. Students read a short poem aloud, practising pronunciation and identifying words with the 'ay' and 'oy' sounds in context.
Look for confident reading, accurate pronunciation of the target words, and a good sense of the poem's rhythm.
“Our job isn’t done yet, detectives.  Let’s read this poem together. While we read, can you use your detecting ears again and listen for all the special 'ay' and 'oy' words hiding in it?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.117-119 - B Circle ay words in red and oy words in blue

details: Circle... reinforces grapheme recognition and categorization. Students scan the text to find the target words and circle them in the correct colour to show they can differentiate the spellings.
Look for accurate identification of all target words and correct use of the colours for the two different spelling patterns.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down:
